newsitem.title: UK: UK MPs see delay to competitive electricity market.
newsitem.headline: UK MPs see delay to competitive electricity market.

text.p: Liberalisation of Britain's electricity market has fallen behind schedule and could be delayed, parliament's Trade and Industry Committee said on Thursday.
The committee said in a report that OFFER, the market regulator, and the electricity supply industry had made significant progress in preparing for a competitive market.
"But given they will have had eight years notice...this progress is substantially less than we would have expected to see some 12 months before implementation," the committee's report said.
The report said completing the programme of freeing up the electricity market by April 1, 1998 -- its target date -- "represents an enormous challenge".
"Given the outstanding problems...the possibility of a short delay to the start date should not be excluded," it said.
The committee said full-scale liberalisation in 1998 should offer some 25.8 million customers a choice of supplier, compared with the 45,000 who can currently pick from more than one provider.
But the success of a fully competitive electricity market is dependent upon information systems being fully tested and ready for operation by April next year.
The committee said several electricity companies had assured it that their systems would be up and running but said if others were not, the whole system could crumble.
The report quoted London Electricity's warning that the risk of delay was high.

"Given the integrated nature of the industry's preparations, where failure by one party or lack of coordination between parties may defeat the whole programme, we believe the risk that the industry will not be ready by April 1, 1998 is very high," a London Electricity statement said.

The MPs also noted the concerns of British Gas. It said that if gas supply liberalisation went ahead on time but the electricity industry was allowed to delay, electricity suppliers could then offer consumers combined gas and electricity services but British Gas could not.
That could cause "serious market distortions" British Gas said.

"On the evidence available to us, we do not believe that it would be justified to recommend postponement at present," the Trade and Industry Committee said. "But we have serious reservations about the likelihood of information systems being ready on time.

The committee urged the director general of electricity supply to come up with workable contingency plans in case some of the electricity companies fail to meet the deadline. "He should not hesitate to announce a short postponement should he judge it necessary," it said.
"But it is important that all parties remain fully committed and willing to work together," the MPs concluded.
